Empire Taff was a steel-hulled cargo steamship. She was built in Germany in 1927 for Dampfschifffahrts-Gesellschaft „Neptun“ as Apollo. In 1945 the United Kingdom seized her as war reparations, and renamed her Empire Taff. In 1947 the UK government sold her to a Scottish shipping company, which renamed her ''. She was scrapped in Scotland in 1953.
She was the second of three  ships to be named after the ancient Greek god Apollo. The first was an iron-hulled steamship that was built  by Möller & Holberg, Stettin, in 1883,requisitioned by the Imperial German Navy in 1914,  and last recorded in Lloyd's Register in 1920. The third was a motor ship that was built by Nobiskrug GmbH, Rendsburg, West Germany in 1957, sold and renamed Peliki in 1972, and scrapped in 1984.
Ajax-class cargo ships
In 1927, AG Weser in Bremen built a class of four cargo steamships for  (the "Neptune Steamship Company"). Yard number 866 was launched as Ajax; 867 as Apollo; 868 as Atlas; and 869 as Arion. Each had a single screw, and their main engine was a three-cylinder triple-expansion engine.
Each Ajax-class ship had also a Bauer-Wach exhaust steam turbine, which Gustav Bauer and Hans Wach at Joh. C. Tecklenborg in Bremerhaven had patented in 1926. Tecklenborg and AG Weser had then become two of the constituents of DeSchiMAG, and Tecklenborg shared the patented system within the DeSchiMAG group.
Apollo
Apollos registered length was ; her beam was , and, as built, her depth was . Her tonnages were  and . The combined power of her reciprocating engine plus her turbine was rated at 180 NHP, or 1,170 ihp. She was equipped with submarine signalling.  registered her at Bremen. Her code letters were QMGD.
By 1930,  had each ship of the Ajax class altered to increase their depth from  to . This increased Apollos tonnages to  and . By 1934, her wireless telegraph call sign was DOKF, and this had superseded her code letters. Her navigation equipment was augmented with the addition of an echo sounding device in 1937, and wireless direction finding in 1938.
Empire Taff and Ahama
In May 1945, the UK seized Apollo as a war prize at Flensburg. The Ministry of War Transport took ownership of her, and renamed her Empire Taff, after the River Taff in south Wales. She was registered in London; her UK official number was 180673; and her call sign was GNFN. McAndrews & Co of London were her managers.
In 1947, the MoWT sold the ship to John Bruce & Co, who renamed her Alhama, and registered her in Glasgow. She was scrapped in 1953, at Faslane in Argyll.
